title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: In one-hot encoding, each category is represented by a binary vector. For the 'meat' variable, 'beef', 'chicken', and 'fish' are encoded as separate binary variables. Only one of these variables can be $$1$$ at a time, while the others are $$0$$.

title: Interpreting the Box Plot
text: The box plot shows the distribution of total costs for each type of meat. Compare the median and spread of the costs for 'beef', 'chicken', and 'fish'.

title: Analyzing the Model Weights
text: The weight $$\theta_2$$ corresponds to the $$'meat=chicken'$$ variable. Consider how the cost of chicken compares to the other meats based on the box plot.

title: Comparing Costs
text: Based on the box plot, is the cost of chicken generally higher, lower, or about the same as beef and fish?

title: Determining the Sign of $$\theta_2$$
text: If the cost of chicken is generally lower than the other meats, what does this imply about the sign of $$\theta_2$$?
